summary: Played live (follow, orbit, free cameras; Firefly catch and Berry race through interact!, dusk to night) and compared with s20/s35/s36 progress shots. By day the clay-toy island is cozy and the pier chat with a fishing Sprout is the best frame in the game, but the island geometry is unchanged since session 20, the sea is a flat grey slab with a sawtooth horizon, dusk/night play is dark, and some critters sit 'off to the berry bushes' for hours. The mini games are clear and winnable but are counters; nothing yet is a moment to show a friend.

lighting.why: Day is clean; orbit-b.png shows flat grey sea and a hard sawtooth horizon; at 17:18-19:36 the pier and forest fall to near black (pier-chat shot, br-end.png), though the lantern pool at 19:19 (br-start.png) is lovely.

world.why: Overview of s36 vs s20: same hill, pond, path and pier, more trees; no new area in 16 sessions; sea is a slab.

props.why: Generated trees, mushrooms, tufts, signpost and cottage share a clay look; little grouping into scenes (camp, garden, market) and rocks are generic.

creatures.why: Hats, a beret, notes and hearts add charm (br-start.png 'Whee, dizzy!'), but bodies are blobs and Pickles/Sir Sniffsalot read 'off to the berry bushes' at 13:26, 16:14, 16:33 and 19:19.

fun.why: Played both: Firefly catch has a clear card, key hints and a live '7 m to your left' cue (good); Berry race showed 'You 0 - Critters 2' after 15 s in a dark top-down view. Still counters, no moment to show a friend.

camera.why: Follow on the pier (follow-a.png) and the fishing chat (ff-mid at 17:18) frame well; orbit/free show a flat grey sea and empty sky band; Berry race top-down at night is dark with Sprout tiny; eye-level progress shot is identical in s35 and s36.

ui.why: Panel text is stale: Sprout shows 'walking the whole island with a critical eye' while the player is in a mini game, 'New on the island: The carried pebble is hard to see' and a changelog message stay for hours; right column half empty; HUD pill in mini games is good.

style.why: Clay-toy look is cohesive in raster and traced still; the traced still shows a jagged horizon band and noisy fur and the browser look differs.

performance.why: 30 fps, median frame about 3 ms reported by the author.

findings.title: A shareable moment: creatures play a game together and Sprout joins
findings.what: Interactions are counters (catch 8 fireflies, race to berries) and one-off emotes. Nothing emerges between creatures that a player would want to show someone.
findings.where: plugins: mini games, cairns, ballplay, dancecircle
findings.evidence: world/reviews/p36/ff-mid.png (17:18): Sprout fishing and chatting with Truffle on the pier is the one frame that tells a story; mini games show only counters
findings.suggestion: Grow that pier chat into an event: creatures gather with their own props (rod, lantern, picnic), react to each other with distinct emotes, Sprout joins with E. Frame it with a group camera and make it visible in the world afterwards.
findings.done_when: A 20 s clip of the event shows at least 4 creatures reacting distinctly, and the play test shows Sprout joining changes what the others do.

findings.title: Creatures with real silhouettes: limbs, ears, tails, walk cycles
findings.what: Most critters are spheres with stub legs; at overview distance the pig and sheep are only blobs and Sprout is a white egg seen from behind.
findings.where: creature species code, progress overview.png and dashboard.png
findings.evidence: media/progress/session-0036/dashboard.png (Sprout egg) vs releases/.../still.png (sheep with face reads better).
findings.suggestion: Give each species a distinct silhouette (long ears, tail, snout, wool tufts), a bounce walk with squash and stretch, and idle behaviours (scratch, yawn, look at flowers). Generate head or body meshes as assets.
findings.done_when: Cropped screenshots of three species at overview distance are told apart without name tags; a walk cycle visible in a 1 s frame strip.

findings.title: A second and third place: flower meadow and beach with their own props
findings.what: The whole island is one grass hill; the sea is a dark slab. Nothing to walk toward.
findings.evidence: media/progress/session-0036/overview.png: uniform green with trees scattered, black-navy sea.
findings.suggestion: Make 2-3 clearly different regions (sandy cove with driftwood and shells, flower meadow with butterflies, mossy rock grove) with their own colours and props, and lit paths between them.
findings.done_when: Overview screenshot shows at least three differently coloured regions; each has 5+ props unique to it.

findings.title: Creatures that get stuck: 'off to the berry bushes' for hours
findings.what: Pickles and Sir Sniffsalot are listed as 'off to the berry bushes' at 13:26, 16:14, 16:33, and again at 19:19: they appear to be stuck on the way, never arriving. A player watching sees creatures not living.
findings.where: On the island now panel, berry race / wild race goals
findings.evidence: world/reviews/p36/follow-a.png, orbit-b.png, br-start.png (same two names across 6 game hours); progress shot session-0036 dashboard.png
findings.suggestion: Find why they never arrive (path blocked by trees/Separation, goal never reaching berries), give every goal a timeout and re-pick, and log creatures whose goal lasts over 90 s as a test failure.
findings.done_when: A 30 min live sample shows no creature with the same goal longer than 2 min; a test asserts it.

findings.title: Soft sea and a gradient horizon with no jagged band
findings.what: Sea is a flat navy slab in the raster and the traced still shows a jagged grey sawtooth along the horizon.
findings.where: sea mesh, horizon; releases still.png at y=240
findings.evidence: world/reviews/p36/orbit-b.png and free-a.png: flat grey slab, hard sawtooth line at the horizon; releases still.png shows the same band
findings.suggestion: Fix the horizon band (see todo 131), add depth colour from shore to open water, foam at the beach, sky reflection.
findings.done_when: Traced still and raster overview show no sawtooth and a visible shore-to-deep gradient.

findings.title: Dusk and night that look cozy: lit windows, lanterns, warm pools
findings.what: Night ground is near black with hard shadow blobs; the cottage and lanterns give too little light.
findings.evidence: world/reviews/p36/ff-mid.png (17:18 pier nearly black), br-end.png (19:36 forest black, Sprout tiny top-down); br-start.png lantern pool shows what works
findings.suggestion: Warm lit windows on the cottage, lantern pools, blue moon fill and a lifted ambient so shapes read.
findings.done_when: Mean luminance of the 3D area at 23:00 is above a set threshold and a night screenshot shows warm pools around 3 light sources.

findings.title: Cameras with a subject: eye-level, orbit and night Berry race
findings.what: The eye-level progress shot frames empty grass and tufts; no creature in view. Overview is a generic orbit.
findings.evidence: world/reviews/p36/orbit-a/b.png (sea and sky, island small), br-end.png (top-down dark); media/progress eye-level.png identical in s35 and s36
findings.suggestion: Eye-level cameras pick a creature or event, use a low angle with foreground framing and depth of field feel; overview orbits slowly with a target.
findings.done_when: Three random eye-level shots over a day each contain a creature taking more than 5% of the frame.

findings.title: Dashboard panel: a live picture of the island instead of changelog text
findings.what: Right panel is half empty; 'New on the island: The carried pebble is hard to see' and the 'Messages to you' changelog read as dev notes; the list of creatures is text. Sprout's status line says 'walking the whole island with a critical eye' even while the player plays a mini game.
findings.evidence: world/reviews/p36/follow-a.png: stale Sprout status + 'carried pebble' note; dashboard half empty
findings.suggestion: Creature portraits with mood icons, a small island map with dots, a friendship or cairn counter; messages short and for a player.
findings.done_when: Dashboard shows portraits and a mini map; no panel contains the words pebble/tested/session.

process: The author has shipped goal 2's first release and keeps good evidence habits, but sessions 35-36 went into the cairn (carry offset, camera group) and worker plumbing, while the dominant things a player sees, creature silhouettes, the sea, the night and a second area, barely moved in three reviews. Goal 1 gets small increments instead of one big event; goal 3 improved the day look but night and the sea lag. Next sessions should spend whole sessions on creatures, a new area and the night, with before/after screenshots. Live check: the sim moves 24 game minutes per day, so a first look at the game at dusk (when most players arrive) is dark; spend a session on dusk/night readability.
